claim: The M2 proton channel aids in the exit of mature influenza viral particles from the host plasma membrane through its ability to stabilize regions of high negative Gaussian curvature (NGC) that occur at the neck of budding virions.
source: The M2 proton channel aids in the exit of mature influenza viral particles from the host plasma membrane through its ability to stabilize regions of high negative Gaussian curvature (NGC) that occur at the neck of budding virions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary function of M2, supported by the study's findings.

claim: M2 channels are homo-tetramers that contain a cytoplasm-facing amphipathic helix (AH) that is necessary and sufficient for NGC generation.
source: The channels are homo-tetramers that contain a cytoplasm-facing amphipathic helix (AH) that is necessary and sufficient for NGC generation
evidence: This structural and functional claim is stated in the abstract.

claim: Constructs containing the transmembrane spanning helix, which facilitates tetramerization, exhibit enhanced curvature generation compared to the AH alone.
source: however, constructs containing the transmembrane spanning helix, which facilitates tetramerization, exhibit enhanced curvature generation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a comparative observation.

claim: The AH domain of M2 is dynamic and quickly breaks the fourfold symmetry observed in most structures.
source: Here, we used all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to explore the conformational dynamics of M2 channels in lipid bilayers revealing that the AH is dynamic, quickly breaking the fourfold symmetry observed in most structures.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the MD simulations reported in the abstract.

claim: All M2 configurations induced pronounced curvature in the outer leaflet, while the inner leaflets showed minimal curvature and significant lipid tilt around the AHs.
source: While each pattern was distinct, all configurations induced pronounced curvature in the outer leaflet, while conversely, the inner leaflets showed minimal curvature and significant lipid tilt around the AHs.
evidence: This is a key finding from the MD simulations described in the abstract.

claim: All three M2 conformations are stabilized in inward-budding, concave spherical caps and destabilized in outward-budding, convex spherical caps.
source: The calculations show that all three M2 conformations are stabilized in inward-budding, concave spherical caps and destabilized in outward-budding, convex spherical caps, the latter reminiscent of a budding virus.
evidence: This is a primary result from the continuum elastic membrane model calculations.

claim: One of the C2-broken symmetry conformations is stabilized by 4 kT in NGC surfaces with the minimum energy conformation occurring at a curvature corresponding to 33 nm radii.
source: One of the C2-broken symmetry conformations is stabilized by 4 kT in NGC surfaces with the minimum energy conformation occurring at a curvature corresponding to 33 nm radii.
evidence: This is a specific quantitative result from the continuum model calculations.

claim: M2 is a small, α-helical homo-tetrameric membrane protein essential for viral replication.
source: Influenza A M2 is a small, α-helical homo-tetrameric membrane protein essential for viral replication (Rossman and Lamb, 2011).
evidence: This is a basic characterization of M2 supported by citation.

claim: During cell entry via endocytosis, endosomal acidification activates M2 channels causing further acidification that releases bound viral ribonucleoproteins (vRNP) to enter the host's cytoplasm.
source: First, during cell entry via endocytosis, endosomal acidification initiates fusion of the endosomal and viral membranes, but it also activates M2 channels causing further acidification that releases bound viral ribonucleoproteins (vRNP) to enter the host's cytoplasm (Pielak and Chou, 2011).
evidence: This describes one of M2's primary functions with citation support.

claim: During capsid exit from the cell, M2 channels residing in the host plasma membrane migrate to the budding virion where they enrich at the neck region and promote membrane scission.
source: Second, during capsid exit from the cell, M2 channels residing in the host plasma membrane migrate to the budding virion where they enrich at the neck region and promote membrane scission resulting in the release of the mature membrane enveloped viral particle (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes M2's second primary function with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: M2-deletion mutants are replication impaired, resulting in accumulation of ~25 nm blebs on the host membrane that only rarely resolve into infectious particles.
source: Consequently, M2-deletion mutants are replication impaired, resulting in accumulation of ~25 nm blebs on the host membrane that only rarely resolve into infectious particles (Rossman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an experimental observation cited from the literature.

claim: M2 plays the main part in ESCRT-independent scission of nascent viral buds by promoting further constriction of the existing ~25 nm neck.
source: While other influenza factors are involved in viral egress, M2 seems to play the main part in ESCRT-independent scission of nascent viral buds by promoting further constriction of the existing ~25 nm neck in order to facilitate spontaneous membrane scission, and thus determines the shape of the mature virion (i.e., spherical or filamentous) (Martyna et al., 2017; Rossman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a functional claim supported by citations.

claim: The M2 protein is 97 residues long with largely disordered N- and C-termini connected by a single pass transmembrane (TM) α-helical segment (residues 23–46) and an amphipathic helix (AH; residues 47–62).
source: The M2 protein is 97 residues long with largely disordered N- and C-termini connected by a single pass transmembrane (TM) α-helical segment (residues 23–46) and an amphipathic helix (AH; residues 47–62) called the AH domain.
evidence: This is a structural description of M2.

claim: A minimal-construct 'conductance domain' (CD) comprised of the TM and AH domains is both ion channel competent and sufficient for budding.
source: Channels are homo-tetrameric assemblies with the ion conduction pathway formed at the center of the four TM helices, and a minimal-construct 'conductance domain' (CD) comprised of the TM and AH domains is both ion channel competent and sufficient for budding (Sharma et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a functional characterization supported by citation.

claim: The cytoplasm-facing AH domain is essential for scission activity.
source: The cytoplasm-facing AH domain is essential for scission activity (Roberts et al., 2013)
evidence: This is a functional claim supported by citation.

claim: M2 chimeras with genetically unrelated amphipathic helices are scission-competent and promote viral replication in vivo.
source: but M2 chimeras with genetically unrelated amphipathic helices are scission-competent and promote viral replication in vivo (Hu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by citation.

claim: The N- and C-termini of M2 are not essential for bud localization, negative Gaussian curvature (NGC) generation, or scission.
source: Meanwhile, the N- and C-termini are not essential for bud localization, negative Gaussian curvature (NGC) generation, or scission (Chen et al., 2008; Kwon and Hong, 2016; Martyna et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a functional claim supported by multiple citations.

claim: All M2 structures reveal channels composed of four α-helical TM segments, with varying degrees of TM helix tilt with respect to the central axis.
source: All structures reveal channels composed of four α-helical TM segments, with varying degrees of TM helix tilt with respect to the central axis.
evidence: This is a structural observation from multiple structures.

claim: The TM helices exhibit greater splay on the cytoplasmic/intraviral side of the membrane than on the extracellular/extraviral surface giving rise to a conically shaped membrane spanning region.
source: Generally, the helices exhibit greater splay on the cytoplasmic/intraviral side of the membrane than on the extracellular/extraviral surface giving rise to a conically shaped membrane spanning region.
evidence: This is a structural observation from multiple structures.

claim: Helix kinking at glycine 34 has been suggested to control the degree of splay in active (greater) and inactive (lesser) conformations in a pH-dependent manner.
source: Helix kinking at glycine 34 has been suggested to control the degree of splay in active (greater) and inactive (lesser) conformations in a pH-dependent manner, which consequently increases and decreases, respectively, the conical character of the protein (Stouffer et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis supported by citation.

claim: Crystal structure constructs lack the entire AH domain and hence provide limited use in understanding the full membrane deforming function of the protein.
source: Unfortunately, crystal structure constructs lack the entire AH domain and hence provide limited use in understanding the full membrane deforming function of the protein Schmidt et al., 2013
evidence: This is an assessment of the limitations of crystal structures with citation.

claim: The AH domain is the most variable part of the CD.
source: however, several structures (mostly ssNMR) have resolved this portion revealing that it is the most variable part of the CD (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a structural observation from multiple structures with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Most M2 studies reveal that the backbone adopts a roughly fourfold symmetric channel.
source: Most studies reveal that the backbone adopts a roughly fourfold symmetric channel
evidence: This is a general observation from structural studies.

claim: An ssNMR structure of a seasonal variant of M2 provided spectroscopic evidence for a twofold symmetric tetramer in which the AH domains break fourfold symmetry.
source: however, an ssNMR structure of a seasonal variant of M2 provided spectroscopic evidence for a twofold symmetric tetramer (Andreas et al., 2015) in which the AH domains break fourfold symmetry (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a structural finding supported by citation and Figure 1B.

claim: DEER experiments support the notion that the AH domains are dynamic with a high degree of flexibility.
source: Moreover, double electron–electron resonance (DEER) experiments support the notion that the AH domains are dynamic with a high degree of flexibility (Herneisen et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by citations.

claim: M2 channel activity correlates with the degree of helix splay.
source: As stated, while M2 channel activity correlates with the degree of helix splay, we focus in this manuscript exclusively on the shape of the M2 protein and not its channel activity.
evidence: This is a known correlation stated in the introduction.

claim: The conically shaped CD construct is wedge-like, displacing more membrane area on the cytoplasmic leaflet than the extracellular leaflet, imparting a spontaneous curvature on the membrane.
source: This mechanism is also relevant for M2 as the conically shaped CD construct is wedge-like, displacing more membrane area on the cytoplasmic leaflet than the extracellular leaflet, imparting a spontaneous curvature on the membrane that agrees with the estimated curvatures at the budding neck (Schmidt et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation supported by citation.

claim: The nascent bud is cholesterol and sphingomyelin rich.
source: Finally, the nascent bud is cholesterol and sphingomyelin rich (Gerl et al., 2012; Ivanova et al., 2015)
evidence: This is a compositional characterization supported by citations.

claim: M2 and other membrane scission proteins have been shown to be 'linactants' that modify line tension.
source: M2 and other membrane scission proteins have been shown to be 'linactants' that modify line tension (Kuzmin et al., 2005)
evidence: This is a functional characterization supported by citation.

claim: A recent simulation study of M2 crowded into a bilayer patch showed the emergence of linear clusters and attendant changes in membrane curvature.
source: A recent simulation study of M2 crowded into a bilayer patch showed the emergence of linear clusters and attendant changes in membrane curvature (Paulino et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a simulation finding supported by citation.

claim: Experiments show that M2 binds cholesterol sub-stoichiometrically with two proximal (as opposed to diagonal) lipids per M2 tetramer.
source: A molecular mechanism supporting M2's role as a linactant comes from experiments showing that M2 binds cholesterol sub-stoichiometrically with two proximal (as opposed to diagonal) lipids per M2 tetramer (Elkins et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by citation.

claim: The neck of a budding vesicle is a catenoid or saddle-like membrane structure characterized by two, orthogonal principal curvatures, κ1 and κ2, of opposite sign.
source: However, the neck is a catenoid or saddle-like membrane structure characterized by two, orthogonal principal curvatures, κ1 and κ2, of opposite sign (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a geometric description with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Recent coarse-grained simulations using a fourfold symmetric model of M2 found that M2 migrated to patches of positive Gaussian curvature rather than the expected NGC regions.
source: Recent coarse-grained simulations by Voth and coworkers using a fourfold symmetric model of M2 support this notion, as they found that M2 migrated to patches of positive Gaussian curvature rather than the expected NGC regions (Madsen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a simulation finding supported by citation.

claim: Unrestrained, all-atom MD simulations of the M2 channel identified large conformational changes in the AH domain that broke fourfold symmetry.
source: Here, we initiated unrestrained, all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the M2 channel and identified large conformational changes in the AH domain that broke fourfold symmetry.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the unrestrained MD simulations.

claim: The TM domain remained stable throughout the 2750 ns simulation with an RMSD ~1 Å.
source: In contrast, the TM domain (yellow) remained stable throughout the 2750 ns simulation with an RMSD ~1 Å.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the MD simulation.

claim: The dynamic nature of the AH helices provides a picture much closer to the experimental DEER values.
source: The dynamic nature of the AH helices provides a picture much closer to the experimental values, as proposed by the Howard lab (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the MD results in comparison to experimental data.

claim: The simulations confirm that the AH domains are flexible and can adopt many conformations, some of which break the fourfold symmetry of the channel.
source: Our unbiased simulations confirm that the AH domains are flexible and can adopt many conformations, some of which break the fourfold symmetry of the channel.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the unbiased MD simulations.

claim: Reorientation of the AH domains in a flat bilayer requires little energy and may be favorable, as it occurs spontaneously on a short timescale (microseconds).
source: The simulations also suggest that reorientation of the AH domains in a flat bilayer requires little energy and may be favorable, as it occurs spontaneously on a short timescale (microseconds) and in some cases helices return to their starting position (right AH helix in snapshot 2 vs. 3, Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an inference from the MD simulation observations.

claim: Membranes can resolve leaflet asymmetries via lipid flip-flop or curvature generation; however, they cannot be resolved in low-microsecond MD simulations with periodic boundary conditions.
source: Membranes can resolve leaflet asymmetries via lipid flip-flop or curvature generation; however, they cannot be resolved in low-microsecond MD simulations with periodic boundary conditions, giving rise to internal stresses that can alter membrane mechanical properties (Hossein and Deserno, 2020).
evidence: This is a methodological consideration supported by citation.

claim: The initial restrained simulation of 2L0J had a differential tension of −10.8 mN/m in the upper leaflet and 24.6 mN/m in the lower leaflet.
source: From the pressure tensor, we calculated the lateral pressure profile and leaflet tensions arriving at a value of −10.8 mN/m in the upper leaflet and 24.6 mN/m in the lower leaflet (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the pressure tensor analysis with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: The rebalanced simulation with 183 lipids in the lower leaflet and 200 in the upper leaflet restores symmetry to the leaflet tensions.
source: We eventually arrived at a rebalanced condition, with 183 lipids in the lower leaflet and 200 in the upper leaflet, that restores symmetry to the leaflet tensions as can be seen by comparing the pressure profile peaks at z = ±10 Å (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a result from the membrane repacking with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: The membrane shape is one of the most robust features of this system, as changes were minor across the wide range of lower lipid counts explored despite dramatic changes in other membrane properties.
source: The membrane shape is one of the most robust features of this system, as changes were minor across the wide range of lower lipid counts explored despite dramatic changes in other membrane properties, such as tension and lipid shape (see Appendix 1—table 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the membrane repacking studies.

claim: The amphipathic helices exhibited a similar high degree of conformational flexibility and symmetry breaking in repacked, low tension configurations.
source: We performed four independent simulations starting from repacked, low tension configurations and found that the amphipathic helices exhibited a similar high degree of conformational flexibility and symmetry breaking as before (see Appendix 1—figure 4).
evidence: This is a result from additional simulations confirming the robustness of the AH flexibility.

claim: All M2 conformations induce pronounced pinching and large curvature in the extracellular leaflets.
source: The repacked, restrained simulations in three different M2 configurations exhibit common features in the induced membrane distortion patterns. We observed pronounced pinching and large curvature in the extracellular leaflets
evidence: This is a common finding across all three restrained simulations.

claim: The lower leaflet lipids in each simulation experienced greater tilt around the amphipathic helices, with lipid tails 'wrapping' around the partially inserted AH domains.
source: The lower leaflet lipids in each simulation experienced greater tilt around the amphipathic helices, with lipid tails 'wrapping' around the partially inserted AH domains.
evidence: This is a common finding across all three restrained simulations.

claim: The increase in tilt decreases the vertical reach of the lower leaflet lipids, locally lowering the bilayer midplane, and the upper leaflet pinches and bends to accommodate.
source: Consequently, the increase in tilt decreases the vertical reach of the lower leaflet lipids, locally lowering the bilayer midplane, and the upper leaflet pinches and bends to accommodate.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation of the observed membrane deformations.

claim: The AH domains cause upper leaflet bending and compression in patterns that reflect how the individual AH domains are oriented with respect to the stable TM core.
source: Thus, our work suggests that the AH domains cause upper leaflet bending and compression in patterns that reflect how the individual AH domains are oriented with respect to the stable TM core.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the restrained MD simulations.

claim: Both twofold symmetric conformations induce a twofold symmetric deformation that has more upper leaflet pinching and bending along one direction than another.
source: Both twofold symmetric conformations induce a twofold symmetric deformation that has more upper leaflet pinching and bending along one direction than another, while the fourfold symmetric 2L0J simulation creates a more radially symmetric pattern.
evidence: This is a comparative finding from the restrained MD simulations.

claim: The continuum calculations provide an assessment of the membrane distortion energy induced by each conformation in a flat bilayer, with substantial values on the order of 36–115 kT in thick, cholesterol-rich membranes.
source: Our continuum calculations provide an assessment of the membrane distortion energy induced by each conformation in a flat bilayer, and we computed substantial values on the order of 36–115 kT in the thick, cholesterol-rich membranes (~35 Å) simulated here, but more moderate values (15–39 kT) in thinner, cholesterol-free membranes (~28.5 Å).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the continuum model calculations.

claim: The fourfold 2L0J structure has the lowest membrane deformation energy (36 kT), then the twofold 2N70 structure (89 kT), and the largest is the twofold parallel AH domain model (115 kT).
source: Given the significant bilayer compression and induced upper leaflet curvature near the protein boundary, we predict that all three conformations induce significant elastic deformation energy in the bilayer with the fourfold 2L0J the lowest (36 kT), then the twofold 2N70 structure (89 kT), and the largest is the twofold parallel AH domain model (115 kT).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison from the continuum model calculations.

claim: The upper leaflet curvatures produced by all configurations favor migration into concave spherical regions and disfavor convex geometries.
source: The upper leaflet curvatures produced by all configurations favor migration into concave spherical regions and disfavor convex geometries
evidence: This is a conclusion from the continuum model calculations.

claim: The fourfold 2L0J structure does not favor saddle regions of moderate NGC.
source: The fourfold 2L0J structure does not favor saddle regions of moderate NGC
evidence: This is a result from the continuum model calculations.

claim: Only the parallel AH domain model is stabilized in NGC saddles relative to a flat bilayer, while the 2N70 structure is not.
source: However, only the parallel AH domain model is stabilized in NGC saddles relative to a flat bilayer, while the 2N70 structure is not.
evidence: This is a comparative result from the continuum model calculations.

claim: The stabilization energy for the parallel AH model could lead to enrichments in saddles over the flat regions of the plasma membrane by 50- to 400-fold depending on the exact lipid composition.
source: While the stabilization energy for the parallel AH model is modest, it could lead to enrichments in saddles over the flat regions of the plasma membrane by 50- to 400-fold depending on the exact lipid composition of the budding virion (see Figure 11 and Appendix 1—figure 6B)
evidence: This is a quantitative prediction from the continuum model calculations.

claim: C2 symmetry of the membrane deformation pattern appears energetically significant to M2's negative curvature sensitivity.
source: C2 symmetry of the membrane deformation pattern appears energetically significant to M2's negative curvature sensitivity
evidence: This is a conclusion from the continuum model calculations.

claim: The viral membrane lipid composition is quite different from both the plasma membrane and the experimental composition simulated, containing sphingolipids, greater cholesterol content, and enrichment in PE and PS over PC and PG.
source: Another important consideration is that the viral membrane lipid composition is quite different from both the plasma membrane and the experimental composition we mimicked here. We simulated a bilayer containing PC, cholesterol, and negative PG, but the viral envelope has been shown to contain sphingolipids, have greater cholesterol content than what we considered, and be enriched in phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) and phosphatidylserine (PS) over PC and PG, respectively (Gerl et al., 2012; Ivanova et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a compositional comparison supported by citations.

claim: DEER studies suggest that full-length M2 may have a greater propensity to explore C2 conformations than the CD constructs.
source: DEER studies (Herneisen et al., 2017) also suggest that full-length M2 may have a greater propensity to explore C2 conformations than the CD constructs.
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by citation.

claim: The parallel AH domain model was built by starting from the 2N70 structure, removing the unfolded AH domains, and replacing them with one of the folded AH domains from the adjacent subunits.
source: To create this model, we started from the 2N70 structure, removed the unfolded AH domains, and replaced them with one of the folded AH domains from the adjacent subunits.
evidence: This describes the construction method for the parallel AH domain model.

claim: The charged portions of the AH domains fall primarily below the lower surface indicating that they are embedded in the headgroup regions or directly exposed to solution.
source: The charged portions of the AH domains fall primarily below the lower surface indicating that they are embedded in the headgroup regions or directly exposed to solution.
evidence: This is an observation from the MD simulations.

claim: In all three cases, the membrane pinches, or compresses, as it approaches the channel, and this feature is accompanied by a pronounced curvature in the extracellular leaflet, while the cytoplasmic leaflet remains rather flat.
source: In all three cases, the membrane pinches, or compresses, as it approaches the channel, and this feature is accompanied by a pronounced curvature in the extracellular leaflet, while the cytoplasmic leaflet remains rather flat.
evidence: This is a common finding across all three restrained simulations.

claim: For the parallel AH domain model the bilayer is pinched by ~8 Å along the Y-axis, while showing very little compression along the X-axis.
source: Taking the upper and lower deflections together, for the parallel AH domain model the bilayer is pinched by ~8 Å along the Y-axis, while showing very little compression along the X-axis (bottom row, middle panel).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the MD simulations with reference to Figure 5.

claim: The different channel conformations produce distinct local membrane deformation patterns that reflect their individual symmetries and AH orientations.
source: The different channel conformations thus produce distinct local membrane deformation patterns that reflect their individual symmetries and AH orientations, suggesting that such conformational changes may be key to M2 enrichment in the distinct membrane geometries seen in experiment (Rossman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the MD simulations with citation support.

claim: The upper leaflet surface height is strongly deformed around 2L0J, but its thickness is nearly uniform because the midplane surface height mirrors the upper leaflet surface deflection.
source: While the upper leaflet surface height is strongly deformed around 2L0J, its thickness is nearly uniform (top left) because the midplane surface height (lower left) mirrors the upper leaflet surface deflection (Figure 5, upper right).
evidence: This is an observation from the MD simulations with reference to Figure 5.

claim: The midplane heights in each of the twofold cases exhibit extreme variation with pronounced downward deflections separated by 180° above each pair of amphipathic helices.
source: The midplane heights in each of the twofold cases also exhibit extreme variation with pronounced downward deflections separated by 180° above each pair of amphipathic helices (red regions within dashed lines).
evidence: This is an observation from the MD simulations.

claim: These midplane depressions arise because the AHs exclude lipid headgroups, requiring the tails to wrap around the helices to reach the TM segments.
source: These depressions arise because the AHs exclude lipid headgroups, requiring the tails to wrap around the helices to reach the TM segments.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation of the observed midplane deflections.

claim: Lipid tilt occurs to a greater degree in the lower leaflet, arising from a mixture of lipid tail kinking, splaying apart of lipid tails, and simple off-normal tilting.
source: Lipid tilt is apparent throughout; however, it occurs to a greater degree in the lower leaflet, arising from a mixture of lipid tail kinking (e.g., the purple POPC in the 2N70 snapshot), splaying apart of lipid tails (e.g., the purple POPC in the parallel AH domain model snapshot), and simple off-normal tilting of an otherwise 'regular conformation' lipid (e.g., the purple POPG in the 2L0J snapshot).
evidence: This is an observation from the MD simulations.

claim: The simulations failed to identify any cholesterol binding events or hot spots on the low-microsecond timescale.
source: Of note, while we observe cholesterol adjacent to the channel, and cholesterol has been shown to bind M2 (Elkins et al., 2017), our simulations failed to identify any binding events or hot spots on the low-microsecond timescale, which may be the result of the backbone restraints or inadequate sampling.
evidence: This is a negative result from the MD simulations with citation.

claim: The mean tilt far from the protein approaches similar values in the upper and lower leaflets, indicating that lipids near the boundary sample equilibrium, flat bilayer-like conformations.
source: For all three systems, the mean tilt far from the protein approaches similar values in the upper and lower leaflets, indicating that lipids near the boundary sample equilibrium, flat bilayer-like conformations (Figure 7, middle and bottom rows).
evidence: This is an observation from the MD simulations with reference to Figure 7.

claim: The lower leaflets exhibit much more tilt around 30° at the protein and decaying to 15° at the simulation boundary.
source: The highest degree of tilt occurs at the protein–membrane contact curve, and while there is some tilt in the upper leaflet most notably for the twofold parallel AH model (middle column) and 2N70 (right column) structures, the lower leaflets (bottom row) exhibit much more tilt around 30° at the protein and decaying to 15° at the simulation boundary.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the MD simulations.

claim: The tilt pattern in the lower leaflet for the fourfold 2L0J shows a high degree of rotational symmetry; however, the twofold symmetric constructs produce less-rotationally symmetric tilt patterns.
source: The tilt pattern in the lower leaflet for the fourfold 2L0J shows a high degree of rotational symmetry; however, the twofold symmetric constructs produce less-rotationally symmetric tilt patterns.
evidence: This is a comparative observation from the MD simulations.

claim: The 2L0J simulation produces the most isotropic patterning versus distance of the three simulations, with smaller ranges in value of deflection and tilt at fixed distances.
source: As expected from the deflection and tilt surfaces in Figures 5 and 7, respectively, the 2L0J simulation (left column, Figure 8B) produces the most isotropic patterning versus distance of the three simulations, with smaller ranges in value of deflection and tilt at fixed distances and brighter spots consistent with tight clustering.
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of MD simulations with reference to Figures 5, 7, and 8.

claim: All M2 conformations induce large curvature in the upper leaflet with far less curvature in the lower leaflet, while the lipid tilt profiles experience little deviation from a flat bilayer in the upper leaflet and strong deviation in the lower leaflet.
source: Contrasting the height deformation profiles in Figure 5 with the tilt profiles in Figure 7, a striking feature emerges: all M2 conformations induce large curvature in the upper leaflet with far less curvature in the lower leaflet, while the lipid tilt profiles experience little deviation from a flat bilayer in the upper leaflet and strong deviation in the lower leaflet.
evidence: This is a comparative conclusion from the MD simulations with reference to Figures 5 and 7.

claim: The lower leaflet lipids adjacent to the AH domains kink and tilt their tails to wrap around the helices, reducing the vertical extent that the tails can reach across the membrane.
source: At the atomic level, the snapshots in Figure 7 explain how the different M2 channels confer this behavior. The lower leaflet lipids adjacent to the AH domains kink and tilt their tails to wrap around the helices. These deformations reduce the vertical extent that the tails can reach across the membrane
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation from the MD simulations with reference to Figure 7.

claim: The upper leaflet lipids at the protein interface extend and move down to fill any gaps, which produces the pinching observed in the outer leaflet.
source: and the upper leaflet lipids at the protein interface extend and move down to fill any gaps, which produces the pinching observed in the outer leaflet.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation from the MD simulations.

claim: These geometric features are very similar to the curvature stresses induced by antimicrobial peptides, originally proposed by the Huang lab.
source: These geometric features are very similar to the curvature stresses induced by antimicrobial peptides, originally proposed by the Huang lab (Huang et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work supported by citation.

claim: The membrane model is based on a Helfrich energy functional to account for elastic curvature in each leaflet coupled with a 'mattress model' accounting for compression between the leaflets.
source: The membrane model is based on a Helfrich, 1973 to account for elastic curvature in each leaflet coupled with a 'mattress model' accounting for compression between the leaflets (Huang, 1986)
evidence: This describes the theoretical basis of the continuum model with citations.

claim: The correspondence between MD and continuum surfaces is remarkable.
source: Nonetheless, both methods produce smoothly varying heights, and their correspondence is remarkable.
evidence: This is an assessment of the agreement between MD and continuum model results.

claim: The greatest difference between the MD and continuum solutions is likely that the MD has imposed periodic boundary conditions on a moderately sized membrane patch, while the continuum model has no imposed periodicity on a much greater region.
source: However, the greatest difference between the MD and continuum solutions is likely that the MD has imposed periodic boundary conditions on a moderately sized membrane patch, while the continuum model has no imposed periodicity on a much greater region with flat, far-field boundaries twice as large in both linear dimensions.
evidence: This is an analysis of the methodological differences between MD and continuum approaches.

claim: None of the M2 configurations are predicted to be stabilized in outward-budding, convex spherical caps.
source: None of these configurations are predicted to be stabilized in outward-budding, convex spherical caps
evidence: This is a result from the continuum model calculations.

claim: At a radius of 125 Å corresponding to stalled buds observed in EM, the energy values for M2 in convex caps range from 30 to 52 kT higher than the energy in a flat bilayer.
source: At a radius of 125 Å corresponding to stalled buds observed in EM, the energy values range from 30 to 52 kT higher than the energy in a flat bilayer (dashed lines in Figure 11A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the continuum model calculations with reference to Figure 11A.

claim: These calculations corroborate the finding that M2 are not observed in the cap of stalled buds.
source: These calculations corroborate the finding that M2 are not observed in the cap of stalled buds (Rossman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the continuum model calculations supported by citation.

claim: The pinching and membrane slope imposed by the protein on the upper (extracellular) leaflet is opposite to the natural curvature of the convex spherical cap, explaining why the membrane-bending energy is high.
source: Panel D shows the solution for the fourfold 2L0J structure, and it is clear why the membrane-bending energy is high; the pinching and membrane slope imposed by the protein on the upper (extracellular) leaflet is opposite to the natural curvature of the convex spherical cap.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation from the continuum model with reference to Figure 11D.

claim: All of the energies are smaller in magnitude in the thinner, cholesterol-free membrane since the moduli are reduced and the membrane thickness is closer to the hydrophobic thickness of the protein.
source: The general shapes of the curves for saddle and outward-budding convex geometries are similar to those in Figure 11A; however, all of the energies are smaller in magnitude in the thinner, cholesterol-free membrane since the moduli are reduced and the membrane thickness is closer to the hydrophobic thickness of the protein reducing the relative amount of pinching in the upper leaflet.
evidence: This is a result from continuum model calculations with different membrane parameters.

claim: The stabilization of the parallel AH model in NGC is diminished in thinner, cholesterol-free membranes.
source: Additionally, the stabilization of the parallel AH model in NGC is diminished.
evidence: This is a result from continuum model calculations with different membrane parameters.

claim: Proteins are destabilized in thin, concave curved membranes compared to thick, cholesterol-rich membranes.
source: The most notable difference is that proteins are now destabilized in thin, concave curved membranes compared to thick, cholesterol-rich membranes (Appendix 1—figure 6).
evidence: This is a result from continuum model calculations with different membrane parameters.

claim: The mobility of the amphipathic helices appears robust across a range of leaflet tension and packing conditions.
source: This mobility of the amphipathic helices appears robust across a range of leaflet tension and packing conditions, as it is seen in the initial unrestrained simulation (Figure 2) and in the repacked conditions (see Appendix: Section 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion from multiple MD simulations.

claim: The restrained simulations highlight the need for proper balancing of leaflet packing in simulations with highly asymmetric proteins.
source: Our restrained simulations highlight the need for proper balancing of leaflet packing in simulations with highly asymmetric proteins.
evidence: This is a methodological conclusion from the simulation studies.

claim: Twofold symmetry is likely important for stabilization in saddle-like geometries, but it is not sufficient as 2N70 is not stable in NGC surfaces.
source: This twofold symmetry is likely important for stabilization in saddle-like geometries, but it is not sufficient as 2N70 is not stable in NGC surfaces.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the continuum model calculations.

claim: The side-by-side packing of fully folded and inserted AH domains in the parallel AH model appears to enhance the membrane distortion compared to the partially unfolded AH in 2N70.
source: The side-by-side packing of fully folded and inserted AH domains in the parallel AH model appears to enhance the membrane distortion compared to the partially unfolded AH in 2N70, producing stronger lipid tilts and an enhanced saddle-like deflection pattern that is minimized in background saddle shapes.
evidence: This is a comparative conclusion from the MD and continuum model results.

claim: The work corroborates the finding that M2 is not enriched in the convex spherical cap of budding virions.
source: Thus, our work corroborates the finding that M2 is not enriched in the convex spherical cap of budding virions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the continuum model calculations.

claim: The underlying mechanism for curvature preference is a relief of strain or increase in strain depending on the background geometry.
source: Qualitatively our results can be understood in terms of the MD-generated distortion profiles in flat bilayers. The upper leaflet curvatures produced by all configurations favor migration into concave spherical regions and disfavor convex geometries, and the underlying mechanism is a relief of strain or increase in strain depending on the background geometry in a similar spirit to the curvature sensing model proposed by Johnson and co-workers (Fu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation with citation support.

claim: The presence of M2 in saddles would likely stabilize saddle formation.
source: and their presence would likely stabilize saddle formation.
evidence: This is a prediction from the continuum model calculations.

claim: 2L0J may represent M2 in a membrane environment without curvature, whereas 2N70 may represent M2 in a highly curved environment.
source: 2L0J may represent M2 in a membrane environment without curvature, whereas our work follows others (Elkins et al., 2017) in supposing 2N70 may represent M2 in a highly curved environment, one possibly more curved than the physiological case.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the structural states with citation support.

claim: Many differences in M2 structures could be partially accounted for by considering the curvature of the membrane mimetic.
source: Indeed, many differences in M2 structures could be partially accounted for by considering the curvature of the membrane mimetic.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about structural variability.

claim: The increased cholesterol content in viral membranes would rigidify the membrane and enhance many of the energies reported.
source: The increased cholesterol content would rigidify the membrane and enhance many of the energies reported here
evidence: This is a prediction about the effect of cholesterol.

claim: Full-length M2 is likely even more dynamic in the entire C-terminal region to accommodate conformational entropy for the disordered tail.
source: While the structural implications are far from certain, it is likely that the full-length protein is even more dynamic in the entire C-terminal region to accommodate conformational entropy for the disordered tail.
evidence: This is a speculation about full-length M2 dynamics.

claim: Finding higher-affinity ligands for the alternate rimantadine site may yield additional insight into the drugability of M2's membrane-bending function.
source: Finding higher-affinity ligands for this alternate rimantadine site may yield additional insight into the drugability of M2's membrane-bending function.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future drug development.

claim: Cholesterol has been shown to bind at two of the tetramer interfaces, suggesting that specific binding to this shallow groove is possible.
source: Additionally, cholesterol has been shown to bind at two of the tetramer interfaces (Elkins et al., 2017), suggesting that specific binding to this shallow groove is possible.
evidence: This is an experimental finding with citation and inference.

claim: Further studies combining unrestrained MD with continuum energy calculations may be able to find dynamically accessible conformations with low energy in saddle-shaped membranes.
source: Further studies combining unrestrained MD with continuum energy calculations may be able to find dynamically accessible conformations with low energy in saddle-shaped membranes
evidence: This is a suggestion for future research.
